newsitem.title: USA: RUBIN SAYS UPS STRIKE SERIOUS MATTER, TALKS NEEDED.
newsitem.headline: RUBIN SAYS UPS STRIKE SERIOUS MATTER, TALKS NEEDED.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said the strike against United Parcel Service by the Teamsters union was a serious matter and the parties should resume talks.
"I think it's a very serious matter and I think it is extremely important that the parties get back together and that they work their way through these issues," Rubin said on MSNBC television.
Rubin said the Taft-Hartley act, under which President Clinton could intervene in the dispute, had very stringent standards.
He noted that when it was last invoked, 20 years ago, the courts had rejected the president's decision.
Clinton and Labor Secretary Alexis Herman were doing the right thing in putting "enormous" pressure on the company and the union to resolve their differences, Rubin said.
